claims.text: A multi-principal-element, Nb/Ta-enriched BCC high-entropy alloy will exhibit a superconducting transition at cryogenic temperatures.
Increasing the proportions of Nb and Ta will enhance electron-phonon coupling in the alloy.
The initial nearly equiatomic alloy forms a homogeneous, single-phase BCC structure after solid-state synthesis.
The alloy composition can be varied by increasing the relative amounts of Nb and Ta while retaining high-entropy character.
Balanced multi-element mixing produces a single-phase BCC structure.
A homogeneous single-phase BCC structure promotes spatially uniform electron-phonon interactions.
Nb and Ta lattice sites mediate enhanced electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling leads to Cooper-pair formation.
Cooper-pair formation triggers superconductivity below a critical temperature.
The enriched alloys will show a superconducting transition between approximately 2 and 10 K.
The superconducting transition will be detectable through zero electrical resistivity and a Meissner effect.
The critical temperature and transition sharpness depend on Nb/Ta concentration.
Near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys without preferential enrichment of superconducting elements will show no superconducting transition above 10 K.
Phase separation or formation of non-BCC structures may suppress the anticipated superconducting transition.
The optimal Nb/Ta enrichment window and precise superconducting transition temperature are unknown.
Failure to observe either zero resistivity or a Meissner signal below 10 K in all phase-pure Nb/Ta-enriched samples would falsify the hypothesis.
